name: Split-radix power-of-two Fourier transform
definition: For N≥4 a power of two and W=e^(−2πi/N), let E_k, O_k, P_k be DFTs of x_(2n), x_(4n+1), x_(4n+3) respectively; X_k=E_(k mod (N/2))+W^k O_(k mod (N/4))+W^(3k) P_(k mod (N/4)), 0≤k<N.
variables: N power-of-two length; k output index; E,O,P shorter unnormalized DFTs; W primitive root
assumptions: Finite complex vector and consistent negative-exponent convention; direct base cases N=1,2
limitations: Irregular recursion and indexing; arithmetic reduction need not imply runtime improvement
failure_conditions: Incorrect residue classes or phase factors
computation: Recursively split into even and two odd residue classes, reuse subtransform outputs and combine in O(N log N) arithmetic; direct base cases.

source.citation: Duhamel, P. and Hollmann, H. (1984). Split radix FFT algorithm. Electronics Letters 20(1), 14–16. https://doi.org/10.1049/el:19840012

application: General power-of-two Fourier transformation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite complex vector of power-of-two length
mechanism_note: Mixed radix-two/radix-four decomposition of the same DFT; partition into even indices and the two odd residue classes gives the stated phase factors. A Cooley–Tukey variant, not a new distinct algorithm.

name: Chirp Z-transform on a geometric contour
definition: For z_k=A W^(−k), X_k=Σ_(n=0)^(N−1)x_n A^(−n) W^(nk), 0≤k<M; W^(nk)=W^(n²/2) W^(k²/2) W^(−(k−n)²/2) with a consistent square root of W.
variables: N,M positive lengths; A,W nonzero complex contour parameters; k output index
assumptions: Finite complex vector and consistent square-root convention; sufficient convolution embedding
limitations: Off-unit-circle powers may overflow or underflow; conditioning can deteriorate; not a general arbitrary-point transform
computation: Choose q with q²=W. Multiply x_n by A^(−n)q^(n²), convolve with q^(−r²) for signed differences r=−(N−1),…,M−1, and multiply output k by q^(k²); use circular embedding length at least N+M−1.

source.citation: Rabiner, L. R., Schafer, R. W. and Rader, C. M. (1969). The chirp z-transform algorithm and its application. Bell System Technical Journal 48(5), 1249–1292. https://doi.org/10.1002/j.1538-7305.1969.tb04268.x

application: General geometric-contour Z-transform evaluation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite vector, output count and nonzero contour parameters
mechanism_note: Generalizes the Bluestein chirp convolution to geometric contours; A=1, M=N and W=e^(−2πi/N) recover the ordinary DFT. Classified as a variant of the existing convolution mechanism.
